name: input.post_message
description: Non-blocking Win32 `PostMessage` peer of input.send_message. Use when the target's message pump is unresponsive to a synchronous send (PostMessage queues the message and returns immediately).

msg.description: Win32 message identifier. The bridge accepts hex strings (`"0x0010"`) and decimal.

wparam_string.description: UTF-8 string used as wparam when the message expects a string-pointer. Mutually exclusive with `wparam`. PostMessage is async, so the agent must keep the buffer alive until the target consumes the message — agents may impose a stricter contract (decline string-pointer posts) or buffer-lifetime limits.

lparam_string.description: UTF-8 string used as lparam when the message expects a string-pointer. Mutually exclusive with `lparam`. Same async-buffer-lifetime caveat as wparam_string.

x-output-schema.description: Empty body — wire response is the literal `OK 0`. PostMessage's BOOL return only indicates whether the post succeeded (failures surface as ERR), not any meaningful response from the target.

x-implementations.name: post_message
x-implementations.description: Win32 `PostMessageW`. Returns immediately after queuing the message; no wait for wndproc. Failures (target window destroyed, etc.) surface as ERR not_found / ERR invalid_args.

windows-modern.description: PostMessageW. UIPI: cross-IL posts are silently dropped (PostMessage returns success — the message simply never delivers). Same post-check + ERR uipi_blocked path as input.send_message and input.mouse.click.

windows-classic.description: PostMessageW (NT 5+) or PostMessageA (NT 4 / 9x, with input transcoding). No UIPI on classic.
